summary: Approve. I read all 192 lines of review-delta.diff (2b229705..fcf6f2a2) and checked them against history/security-r4.json. Both round-4 minors are fixed. (1) The USER_REFERRAL_IP_RETENTION row in docs/reference/environment-variables.md now says 'A blank value keeps the default', which matches env-descriptions.json and UserPropertiesValidationTest. (2) UserProperties.validateReferral now logs a startup WARN whenever ip-lookback > 0. The WARN names backlog B-1 / F-20261119-03 and the need for a trustworthy client IP from the gateway, and it interpolates only the configured lookback Duration. It logs no IP, hash, salt or other sensitive data. The new test enabledIpCheckWarns shows the WARN fires exactly once when the check is on and not at all when it is off. The retention-warning test now uses lookback 0, so it still checks only the retention WARN. ReferralService only moves the existing lookback > 0 condition into a private ipCheckOn() helper. view, claim and refuseIfAbusive keep the same logic: no activity is recorded, no HMAC is computed and claim_ip_hash is NULL when the check is off. The integration test now checks that the claim row exists with claim_ip_hash IS NULL, which is a stronger assertion than before. The SQL is unchanged and still parameterised. VAPID docs: the new deploy-section entries and the changed rows contain only descriptions, with no key values. VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY carries the secret marker in both the service table and the deploy table, and its source is now '.env + helm'. That is accurate: in the worktree, deploy/aws/helm/ecommerce/values.yaml maps both keys from the app secret (vapid_public_key / vapid_private_key) and Terraform feeds them through modules/secrets. The deploy table also gives VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY the secret marker. That over-marks a public value, which is harmless. The USER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY and USER_REFERRAL_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS rows were only moved to keep the tables sorted; their text is unchanged. The delta has no other security-relevant changes: no endpoints, auth, dependencies, ledger paths or deployment config.
